aspirin.description: Used for pain, fever, and inflammation; low doses reduce platelet stickiness. Can irritate the stomach and increase bleeding risk, especially with other blood thinners or NSAIDs.

warfarin.description: Reduces blood clotting by blocking vitamin K–dependent clotting factors. Narrow therapeutic window; many drugs and foods change its effect. Bleeding is the main risk.

metformin.description: First-line treatment for type 2 diabetes: lowers liver glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity. Can rarely cause lactic acidosis; may need dose caution with kidney problems.

lisinopril.description: Lowers blood pressure and reduces strain on the heart; used for hypertension and heart failure. Watch for cough, high potassium, and kidney function changes.

atorvastatin.description: Lowers LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular risk. Liver enzymes and muscle symptoms are monitored; several drugs affect its blood levels via CYP enzymes.

omeprazole.description: Strongly reduces stomach acid for reflux and ulcers. Long-term use affects absorption of some nutrients and may interact with drugs needing acid for absorption.

amlodipine.description: Relaxes blood vessels for hypertension and angina. Common effects include ankle swelling and flushing. Grapefruit can raise levels modestly.

metoprolol.description: Slows heart rate and reduces blood pressure; used for hypertension, angina, and after heart attacks. Can worsen asthma in susceptible people; avoid abrupt stop.

simvastatin.description: Lowers cholesterol. Many interacting drugs (especially CYP3A4 inhibitors) increase muscle toxicity risk; dosing limits apply with certain combinations.

paracetamol.description: Pain and fever relief. Overdose causes serious liver injury; limit total daily amount and watch combination cold/flu products.

acetaminophen.description: Pain and fever relief. Overdose causes serious liver injury; limit total daily amount and watch combination cold/flu products.

ibuprofen.description: Pain, fever, and inflammation. Increases stomach ulcer and kidney risk; can reduce antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin and raise blood pressure.

amoxicillin.description: Broad-spectrum beta-lactam for many bacterial infections. Allergy (rashes to severe reactions) possible; completes prescribed course unless told otherwise.

ciprofloxacin.description: Treats certain gram-negative and other infections. Tendon, nerve, and blood sugar side effects occur; strong enzyme interactions (e.g. theophylline, warfarin).

digoxin.description: Strengthens heart contraction and controls some arrhythmias. Narrow index: toxicity causes nausea, vision changes, dangerous rhythms; levels and kidney function matter.

clopidogrel.description: Prevents platelets from clumping after stents or stroke prevention. Bleeding risk with other anticoagulants or NSAIDs; effect reduced if not activated by liver enzymes.

fluoxetine.description: Used for depression, anxiety, and related conditions. Serotonin syndrome risk with other serotonergic drugs; long half-life and many CYP interactions.

tramadol.description: Moderate pain relief. Seizure risk and serotonin syndrome when combined with MAOIs, linezolid, or other serotonergics; respiratory depression with sedatives.

lithium.description: First-line for bipolar disorder maintenance. Narrow therapeutic range; dehydration, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics can raise levels and cause toxicity.

methotrexate.description: Low weekly doses for rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis; high doses for cancer. Kidney clearance matters; folic acid often co-prescribed; many interacting drugs.

rifampicin.description: Key drug for tuberculosis; strongly induces CYP450 and P-glycoprotein, lowering levels of many medicines (OCPs, warfarin, some HIV drugs) — interaction hotspot.

rifampin.description: Key drug for tuberculosis; strongly induces many drug-metabolizing enzymes, often reducing levels of anticoagulants, contraception, and transplant drugs.

sertraline.description: Treats depression and anxiety. GI upset and serotonin syndrome risk with linezolid, triptans, or other serotonergic agents; monitor with warfarin.

prednisone.description: Anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive. Raises blood sugar and BP, thins skin, and interacts with warfarin, NSAIDs, and vaccines; taper per clinician plan.

albuterol.description: Relieves bronchospasm in asthma and COPD. Tremor and tachycardia; caution with other stimulants and non–beta-1-selective blockers.

salbutamol.description: Relieves acute wheeze and bronchospasm. Common side effects: tremor, palpitations; watch stacking with other beta agonists.

furosemide.description: Removes fluid in heart failure, edema, and hypertension. Low potassium/magnesium; can raise lithium levels and affect kidney function with NSAIDs.

gabapentin.description: Used for neuropathic pain and seizures. Sedation and dizziness; dose adjusted in kidney disease; additive CNS depression with opioids.

hydrochlorothiazide.description: Lowers blood pressure and treats mild fluid retention. Can lower potassium and sodium; raises uric acid; photosensitivity.

levothyroxine.description: Replaces T4 in hypothyroidism. Take consistently relative to food and supplements (calcium, iron reduce absorption); many drugs alter thyroid labs.

apixaban.description: Prevents and treats clots. Major bleeding risk with other anticoagulants/antiplatelets; strong dual P-gp/CYP3A4 inhibitors raise exposure.

rivaroxaban.description: Used for DVT/PE and stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. Food affects absorption for some doses; enzyme and transporter interactions matter.

phenytoin.description: Controls seizures; narrow therapeutic index. Strong CYP inducer—reduces levels of many drugs; nonlinear kinetics at higher doses.

carbamazepine.description: Treats epilepsy and trigeminal neuralgia. Potent enzyme inducer; serious rash (HLA screening in some populations); hyponatremia possible.

azithromycin.description: Treats respiratory and STIs. QT prolongation risk with other QT drugs; can raise digoxin levels; GI upset common.

clarithromycin.description: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor; markedly raises levels of statins, colchicine, and several others. QT prolongation possible.

ketoconazole.description: Potent inhibitor of many drug pathways; major interaction liability. Hepatotoxicity concern with oral use.

diazepam.description: Anxiolytic, muscle relaxant, seizures. Sedation and respiratory depression with opioids or alcohol; long-acting active metabolites.

morphine.description: Strong pain control. Respiratory depression, constipation, sedation; additive CNS depression with benzodiazepines and gabapentinoids.

codeine.description: Mild–moderate pain and cough. Poor metabolizers get little benefit; ultra-rapid metabolizers risk toxicity—genetics matter.

insulin.description: Lowers blood glucose. Dosing adjusts with meals and activity; risk of hypoglycemia with other antidiabetics, alcohol, and missed meals.

nitroglycerin.description: Relieves angina by reducing preload. Headache and hypotension; dangerous hypotension with PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, etc.).

sildenafil.description: Erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension. Contraindicated with nitrates; caution with alpha blockers and some antihypertensives.

cyclosporine.description: Prevents transplant rejection. Narrow index; many drugs alter levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp; nephrotoxicity.

tacrolimus.description: Immunosuppression after transplant. Therapeutic drug monitoring required; macrolides and azoles frequently raise levels.
